expert_proposals.title: Reverse planner cost direction: raise random_page_cost 1.5->2.5, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Incumbent sits at random_page_cost=1.5 and seq_page_cost=0.8, both below the PostgreSQL defaults (4.0/1.0). r007 pushed them further down (1.1/0.7) and was refuted on TPS in 2 of 3 blocks; the cache-consistent low-cost direction is falsified, so the cost model is over-favoring random index paths relative to the actual cached regime.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets consumes 88% of finite terminal capacity at p50=175us with an Index Scan plan. r007's downward cost move (1.5->1.1, 0.8->0.7) was refuted: TPS fell in blocks 2 and 3. Since reject_harmful is the only falsifying verdict and r007 was inconclusive-but-refuted on the TPS edge, reverse the group direction with equal-or-larger amplitude: raise random_page_cost to 2.5 and seq_page_cost to 1.0. This makes the planner less eager to choose random index paths for the dominant GetUserTweets template, favoring cheaper sequential/bitmap paths and reducing per-call page touches that occupy terminal time.
expert_proposals.query_effect: Planner cost recalibration upward should keep GetUserTweets on a stable, cheaper access path and reduce per-call page touches; plan_evidence currently shows a single Index Scan at cost 8.45.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful transaction TPS if the reversed cost direction reduces GetUserTweets terminal occupancy; bounded because the dominant cost is client-side terminal saturation, not planner choice alone.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 should decrease slightly; overall p95 may be unchanged since it is dominated by the same template.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse of refuted r007 direction (1.5->1.1); 2.5 is between incumbent 1.5 and default 4.0, within safe [1.0,6.0].
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; raising it discourages random index paths

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Reverse of refuted r007 direction (0.8->0.7); 1.0 is the PostgreSQL default, within safe [0.5,2.0].
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; raising it rebalances toward sequential paths

predictions.rationale: Reversed cost direction should reduce per-call page touches for the dominant template.
Tail of the dominant template should follow the p50 improvement if the access path is cheaper.
Freed terminal capacity from the dominant template raises completed-transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the reversed cost direction does not change the GetUserTweets access path, TPS and p50 will be unchanged and the planner is not the bottleneck; the terminal saturation is purely client-side.

If WAL sync latency (0.137ms average, wal_wait anomaly) dominates InsertTweet and indirectly terminal time, TPS will not move with planner costs and the WAL commit-path bundle is the correct next action.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: r007 tested the downward cost direction and was refuted on TPS; reversing with larger amplitude (random_page_cost 1.5->2.5, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0) tests the opposite, untested direction of the same planner mechanism against the incumbent.

nodes.label: Reversed cost model favors cheaper access paths for GetUserTweets

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0 leaves the group-commit window too narrow and the writer flushing per-write, so WAL syncs are not coalesced; wal_waiting_backends.max=1 and sync_average_ms=0.137 persist across all rounds.
expert_proposals.mechanism: WAL sync latency is not the dominant cost (sync_average_ms 0.137, write 0.026, host_io stalls 0), but a persistent wal_wait anomaly shows occasional commit-path queueing. The mandatory wal_commit_path bundle is actionable only on wal_writer_flush_after, commit_delay and commit_siblings (wal_buffers, wal_writer_delay, wal_compression are non-actionable at incumbent). Widening the group-commit collection window to 500us and raising the activation threshold to 3 lets the 5 terminals' commits coalesce into fewer fsyncs, while a 256-block (2MB) writer flush batch stops per-write flushing. This is a bounded amplitude increase over the previously parked r005/r006/r007 values, testing whether larger coalescing reduces the residual wal_wait without adding fixed per-commit stall.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88); reducing commit-path queueing frees a small fraction of terminal time for the read-heavy mix.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1%) if WAL coalescing removes residual commit stalls; neutral if wal_wait is not on the critical path.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 may decrease slightly; GetUserTweets p50/p95 essentially unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window and larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer distinct syncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Freed commit-path capacity raises completed transaction throughput.

alternatives.statement: WAL sync is already cheap (0.137ms) and wal_wait is a rare 1-backend blip; the bundle changes nothing measurable and TPS stays flat.
A 500us commit_delay adds fixed per-commit stall that outweighs coalescing, lowering TPS and raising InsertTweet p95.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves the group-commit window at 100us and writer flushing per-write (flush_after=0), so the persistent wal_wait anomaly is unaddressed. A coherent larger-amplitude bundle on the three actionable knobs tests whether coalescing removes residual commit-path queueing.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs

expert_proposals.title: Coarsest SIRead granularity: max_pred_locks_per_page 2->0, per_relation -2->0
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Predicate-lock promotion thresholds remain at defaults (max_pred_locks_per_page=2, max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2) while max_pred_locks_per_transaction is already 8192; SIRead locks are promoted to coarser page/relation granularity early, adding per-txn lock bookkeeping on the dominant GetUserTweets path.
expert_proposals.mechanism: SERIALIZABLE GetUserTweets dominates terminal capacity (0.88). With max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2, PostgreSQL promotes SIRead locks to page/relation granularity after only 2 page locks, inflating lock bookkeeping per transaction. Setting both to 0 forces the coarsest granularity immediately, minimizing per-txn predicate-lock churn. lock_waiting_backends.max=0 and locks_waiting.max=0 confirm no actual lock contention, so this is bookkeeping cost, not blocking. Prior r005 (2->8, -2->4) was refuted; r006 (2->32, -2->16) untested. The 0-bound is the untested opposite extreme of the same granularity axis.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets SIRead locks stay at coarsest page/relation granularity, reducing per-transaction lock bookkeeping on the dominant path.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase in successful_transaction_tps if predicate-lock bookkeeping is a measurable cost; unchanged if lock churn is negligible.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: Slight decrease in GetUserTweets p99; p50/p95 largely unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; forces coarsest page-level SIRead locking. Prior r005 tested 2->8 (refuted), r006 tested 2->32 (untested); 0 is the untested opposite extreme of the same granularity axis.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest page-level SIRead locking

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; forces coarsest relation-level SIRead locking. Prior r005 tested -2->4 (refuted), r006 tested -2->16 (untested); 0 is the untested opposite extreme.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest relation-level SIRead locking

predictions.rationale: Coarsest SIRead granularity reduces total lock count p95 versus incumbent 2343.
Less per-txn lock bookkeeping trims GetUserTweets tail from 1816us.
Freed terminal capacity from reduced bookkeeping raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If predicate-lock bookkeeping is negligible, locks_total.p95 stays flat and TPS is unchanged, indicating the bottleneck is elsewhere (WAL/terminal).
If coarsest granularity increases false-positive serialization conflicts, server_retry_ratio rises from 0.0.
